dedupe_keys.name: code saturne open source computational fluid dynamics software edf r d

description: code_saturne is a free, open-source computational fluid dynamics solver developed primarily by EDF R&D. The site read on 2026-09-26 gives 29 years of development, about 680 thousand lines of code, 19,272 commits and 30 contributors, and the product page describes a general-purpose CFD solver for industrial and research applications built for massively parallel runs with MPI and optional OpenMP, with domain decomposition through ParMETIS or PT-SCOTCH. It reports routine industrial cases of 10 to 50 million cells, production cases above 200 million cells, runs above a billion cells, and inclusion in the European UEABS benchmark suite. Coverage is general fluid mechanics. The source is on GitHub under the GNU GPL version 2, so it is free to use, with install and download pages, documentation and a forum; the site is hosted by Simvia for EDF. Caveats: large runs need HPC resources and CFD expertise, and plant models are not supplied. Simulation uses are thermal hydraulic and mixing studies of reactor components and cooling systems for safety analysis, and a CFD solver within digital twin workflows. Related records: platform-code-aster-structural-mechanics is EDF's mechanics solver, platform-salome-numerical-simulation handles meshing and coupling, and platform-trust-triocfd-thermohydraulics is CEA's CFD platform.
